gloss: good work; thank you for your hard work

definitions.gloss: good work; thank you for your hard work
definitions.explanation: An expression used to acknowledge someone's effort, commonly used when parting after work or finishing a task.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}もお{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}でした。
examples.english: Thank you for your hard work today.

examples.japanese: お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}、{先|さき}に{帰|かえ}ります。
examples.english: Good work, I'm heading home first.

examples.japanese: 「お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}」「お{疲|つか}れ」
{会議|かいぎ}が{終|お}わって、みんなに「お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}でした」と{言|い}った。
examples.english: After the meeting ended, I said 'good work' to everyone.

examples.japanese: {遅|おそ}くまで{残業|ざんぎょう}した{同僚|どうりょう}に「お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}、{大変|たいへん}だったね」と{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I said to the colleague who worked overtime late, 'Good work, that must have been tough.'

notes:
お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま} is one of the most frequently used expressions in Japanese workplace culture.

FORMS:
- お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}です: polite (colleagues, general)
- お{疲|つか}れ{様|さま}でした: past tense (end of work/meeting)
- お{疲|つか}れ: casual (friends, peers)
- お{疲|つか}れ〜: very casual

USAGE:
- As a greeting when meeting colleagues
- As a farewell after work
- To acknowledge someone's effort
- When finishing a project or meeting

NOTE: Often abbreviated to お{疲|つか}れ or おつ in casual contexts.
